edges.effect_quant: The strongest direct signal comes from a 2014 prospective trial where partially hydrolyzed guar gum shortened mean colon transit time from 57.28 to 45.63 hours and increased spontaneous bowel movements, but other controlled studies have shown smaller or more selective gains.
edges.population: adults or older adults with chronic or functional constipation
edges.mechanism: Partially hydrolysed guar fibre increases stool water, modestly changes fermentation, and can improve transit without the gel heaviness seen with some other fibres, which may reduce laxative dependence in some constipated adults.
edges.summary: The literature supports PHGG as a plausible constipation aid, but it is not a slam dunk. Trials usually show some improvement in transit, laxative use, or stool-related symptoms, yet the signal is less dramatic and more context-dependent than with the strongest osmotic or stimulant options.
edges.caveats: PHGG does not clearly outperform good background dietary fiber in every study, and benefits may show up more in laxative reduction or transit measures than in headline stool-frequency gains. This is a reasonable adjunct rather than a universal first-line fix.
